content.text: Star2026 Georgia G-Day spring game will be streamed on ESPN+/SECN+The Bulldogs' annual spring scrimmage will get started in the afternoon on April 18, and can now be watched at home.Last month, the Georgia Bulldogs confirmed that the annual G-Day scrimmage would take place at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday, April 18. At the time, the announcement noted that the 2026 spring game would not be broadcast or streamed by any platform, but would be covered by the Georgia Bulldogs Radio Network. According to the G-Day schedule on the Georgiadogs.com website, the game will now be streamed by ESPN+/SECN+. There is a listing on ESPN as well, which can be seen here. Information on how to view the game on SEC Network+/ESPN+ can be seen below:SEC Network+ is a complimentary digital platform providing hundreds of additional digital-only events to fans through the ESPN App on connected devices. SEC Network+ is not a television channel. It is accessible with your TV provider credentials and is available via the ESPN app on smartphones, tablets, connected streaming devices, or espn.com/watch. For those with a Smart TV or one of the devices listed here you can download the ESPN app and it will ask you to log in with your TV provider credentials. You may also be able to cast it to your Smart TV from your laptop.For SEC Network authenticated subscribers of AT&T TV, Cox, DIRECTV, DISH Network, fuboTV, Hulu + Live TV, Optimum, Sling TV, Spectrum TV, Suddenlink, Verizon Fios, Xfinity TV, YouTube TV, Vidgo, members of the NCTC, as well as those with access to SEC Network through TV-connected devices, you can watch the game via SEC Network+. If you do not have access to the SEC Network, you can access games via a subscription to ESPN+. SEC Network+ is complementary to SEC Network and part of your subscription with your cable, satellite, or streaming provider. For those who have an Xfinity X1 cable box and SEC Network, you can watch it through your cable box - it should show up on your guide, it will just be streaming vs an actual channel. Tickets for the scrimmage are $10 and went on sale Monday, March 30. Free parking for the scrimmage will be available in select lots beginning at 7 a.m. on game day. The Sanford Stadium gates will open at 10:30 a.m. ahead of the annual lettermen's flag football game, which will begin at 10:45 a.m. Normal home game policies will be in place for the scrimmage, with concessions and merchandise sold throughout the stadium. Smart noted last month that there would be no changes to the actual G-Day game format this year, although he did jokingly tease that one potential cosmetic change was possible."G-Day will stay similar assuming [the health of the team]," Smart said. "It's a long way off, but assuming that we're healthy and we have the number of guys we need to be able to play, G-Day would be a very similar format."G-Day serves as the last of 15 practices during the spring for the Bulldogs. Georgia held its first G-Day game back in 1941, and the 2026 edition of the game will be the 82nd in program history. The Red team has a 44-32-4 record against the Black/White team, with the latest result being the Red team's 34-17 victory last April. G-Day was used as a huge promotional tool for Kirby Smart ahead of his first season as the Bulldogs' head coach. Smart pushed for a "93K Day" at the spring game in April 2016 in an effort to build enthusiasm ahead of a new era of Georgia football. The fans complied with Smart's request, leading to a packed Sanford Stadium for what proved to be a 20-20 tie between the Red and Black teams. NFL Draft 2026: What stands out about Georgia offensive lineman Micah MorrisA closer look at the veteran interior lineman who hopes to hear his name called during the draft.It's officially NFL Draft week for the Georgia Bulldogs.The NFL Draft gets underway on Thursday night with the first of seven rounds. The Bulldogs have a number of players hoping to have their names called in this year's draft. They will join a long list of Dawgs who have gotten the call in recent years, which included 13 players in 2025, eight players in 2024, 10 players in 2023, and 15 players in 2022.Since the draft begins later this week, it's time for our annual draft preview series. This year we'll break down nine Bulldogs who will likely hear their names called and highlight what they'll bring to the table at the next level. Last but not least is Georgia offensive guard Micah Morris, a huge lineman who put his athleticism to use up front for the Bulldogs:WHAT HE BRINGS TO THE NFL (Photo: Tony Walsh/UGAAA) Morris is a big interior offensive lineman at 6-foot-5, 334 pounds, but he proved he was still able to move just fine at his size. His 5.09 40-yard dash was in the 86% of interior lineman per MockDraftable, and his 112-inch broad jump was good for the 94% percentile. Morris was known as a weight room warrior at Georgia, which should be music to the ears of NFL scouts. He was throwing weight around in Athens before he ever got to start, and he continued to impress even as a veteran Bulldog. Morris was a strong run blocker and a more than capable pass protector. Personally, I found him to be most impressive when pulling, as the big man would cover a ton of ground in a hurry to get the job done.PRODUCTION AT GEORGIA(Photo: Kevin C Cox, Getty) Morris was one of many Georgia offensive linemen who patiently waited for his turn to start. Morris played in two games as a true freshman in 2021 then got in on seven games the following season. He rotated in during 13 games in 2023 before making his first career start the following season. He ultimately started in five games that fall and played in 12 altogether. Morris returned for his senior season in 2025 and made the most of it. He started in all 14 games last season and helped the Georgia offense put up 32.1 points, 182.1 rushing yards, and 220.3 passing yards per game. In total, Morris played in 48 games at Georgia and started 19 of them.A QUICK GLIMPSEMonroe Freeling and Micah Morris (Photo: Conor Dillon/UGAAA) There were limited highlights online of Morris. I did want to highlight my favorite play of his collegiate career: the first play from overtime of the Tennessee game: Let's take another look at it. Watch Morris pull to the left to help spring Nate Frazier outside: Morris was trusted to cover a lot of ground when pulling, and this play demonstrated his ability to do so. He also occasionally played fullback on the goal line for Georgia, which was certainly a sight to see. By this point in the draft, it is a total crapshoot. The Jaguars aren't in dire need at guard, but they could certainly use another body or two. The Bulldogs have a number of players hoping to have their names called in this year's draft. They will join a long list of Dawgs who have gotten the call in recent years, which included 13 players in 2025, eight players in 2024, 10 players in 2023, and 15 players in 2022.Since the draft begins later this week, it's time for our annual draft preview series. This year we'll break down nine Bulldogs who will likely hear their names called and highlight what they'll bring to the table at the next level. Next up is Georgia receiver Colbie Young, a big-bodied target who brings more than enough speed to the table:WHAT HE BRINGS TO THE NFL (Photo: Nick Tre. Smith, Getty) Young has excellent size at 6-foot-4, 218 pounds, and he doesn't let it slow him down. He ran the 40 in 4.49 seconds, which is a solid showing — especially at his size. Young is an outside receiver capable of going up and getting the football even in tight coverage. He was a red-zone favorite while at Georgia, though he also had the speed to make plays beyond the 20-yard line. He has, in my opinion, underrated footwork — particularly after the catch — and is a capable blocker as well. Young projects as a Day 3 receiver at the draft. That said, his size and playmaking ability will make him a pick positioned to surprise once he gets to training camp.PRODUCTION AT GEORGIA(Photo: Benjamin Wolk, 247Sports) Young transferred from Miami to Georgia before the 2024 season and played in five games before being suspended due to an arrest on an assault charge. He did not play the rest of the season but stayed on the team, eventually returning to practice in late November. Young reached a plea deal the following January and came back for his final season with the Bulldogs. Young was one of Gunner Stockton's go-to receivers early in the 2025 season before a leg fracture suffered in mid-October left Young on the mend. He missed the next six games before returning for the Sugar Bowl, where he caught 3 passes for 22 yards. Despite missing so much time, Young still finished second on the team in receiving yards (358). In two years at Georgia, Young caught 37 passes for 507 yards and 3 touchdowns.A QUICK GLIMPSE(Photo: Chris Collins, 247Sports) You would think at Young's size that it's a challenge to get open downfield, but that's certainly not the case. He was able to create explosive plays downfield quite a bit, like this one against Tennessee: Let's watch the play again. Pay attention to how Young shows his hands late to not allow the Tennessee DB a chance to make a play on the ball: Young makes an Alabama DB look silly with a sluggo that gives him a ton of space downfield: One head fake was all it took for Young to be off to the races there: Young suffered a leg fracture at the end of another big catch downfield: Young does a great job of getting outside and, again, getting his hands up late to make an explosive catch: Something else that is undeniable about Young's game: He will fight for extra yards over and over. Here's an example against Alabama: And here's another example against Auburn: Young's willingness to fight for more yardage and his slippery nature should land him on the radar for teams by Day 3: LATEST PROJECTIONS(Photo: © Ayrton Breckenridge/Clarion Ledger, Getty) ESPN's Mel Kiper: Not included in 2-round mock CBS Sports' Pete Prisco: Not included in 1st round mock The Ringer's Danny Kelly: Not included in 1st round mock Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer: Not included in 7-round mockMY PREDICTION (Photo: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire, Getty) Young goes 190th overall (6th round) to the New Orleans Saints. Like Bell, I see Young going to a team that needs a lot of help at receiver — and might take multiple guys to improve that room. I expect the Saints to pick a receiver as early as eighth overall. They would be wise to circle back later in the going and take a chance on Young.PREVIOUS BREAKDOWNSNFL Draft 2026: What stands out about Georgia receiver Dillon BellTaking a closer look at the veteran receiver and what he brings to the professional level.It's officially NFL Draft week for the Georgia Bulldogs.The NFL Draft gets underway on Thursday night with the first of seven rounds. The Bulldogs have a number of players hoping to have their names called in this year's draft. They will join a long list of Dawgs who have gotten the call in recent years, which included 13 players in 2025, eight players in 2024, 10 players in 2023, and 15 players in 2022.Since the draft begins later this week, it's time for our annual draft preview series. This year we'll break down nine Bulldogs who will likely hear their names called and highlight what they'll bring to the table at the next level. Next up is Georgia receiver Dillon Bell, who played many roles for the Bulldogs and is hoping to do the same at the next level:WHAT HE BRINGS TO THE NFL (Photo: Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire, Getty) Bell isn't the biggest receiver prospect at 6-foot, 209 pounds, but he can hold his own as a blocker and brings the physical nature you need to fight for the football. His 4.5 40 time at the combine showed he has adequate speed, and he demonstrated his athleticism by recording a 39-inch vertical jump. Bell is an adequate route runner who has solid hands as a receiver. While perhaps just short of a contested catch specialist, Bell consistently got the upper hand in one-on-one battles and had a penchant for delivering tough receptions. Perhaps what will make him most attractive as a draft prospect is how he chipped in at running back for the Bulldogs and also took jet sweeps. Bell drew comparisons to Deebo Samuel by his sophomore season at Georgia. While he won't go off the board in the second round like Samuel did, it's easy to see how an NFL front office could make the comparison and pounce on Bell.PRODUCTION AT GEORGIA(Photo: Chris Collins, 247Sports) Bell was thrown into the fire early on at Georgia thanks partly to AD Mitchell dealing with an ankle injury. Bell started five games and played in all 15 for the Bulldogs that year, ending the season with 20 receptions for 180 yards and 3 touchdowns. Bell helped the Bulldogs in the backfield early in his sophomore season due to injury issues at the position. He rushed 25 times for 157 yards and 2 touchdowns while also catching 29 passes for 355 yards and 2 touchdowns. He ended the year with a bang by catching 5 passes for 86 yards in the Bulldogs' blowout win over Florida State in the Orange Bowl. Bell's most productive season came in 2024, when he caught 43 passes for 466 yards and 4 touchdowns. He helped the Bulldogs take a late lead against Alabama thanks to a career-long 67-yard touchdown grab. Unfortunately for the Bulldogs, the Crimson Tide quickly responded to re-take the lead. Whether it was due to a new quarterback or a revamped receiver room, Bell wasn't nearly as productive during his senior season. He racked up 27 receptions for 268 yards and 2 touchdowns. Bell left Georgia with 119 career receptions for 1,269 yards and 11 touchdowns. He also took 51 carries for 373 yards and 5 scores.A QUICK GLIMPSE (Photo: Todd Kirkland, Getty) Bell's greatest strength as a receiver is his contested catch ability. Bell came through in one-on-one situations quite a few times, including on this play against Kentucky: Here's another look at that one-handed snag: Bell delivered an important contested catch late in the going against Ole Miss in October: Bell was interfered with on the play, but that didn't stop him from hauling in the pass: Sticking with his receiving skills, Bell does a good job on this play of going up for the ball and bringing it into his body to secure the catch: Now let's talk about Bell's rushing ability. Bell was used quite a bit on sweeps this past season, and he made the most of many of those opportunities. Watch him turn on the jets on that fake reverse against Alabama: Bell played some running back in high school, and in my opinion it's evident by how he follows his blocks on this play: This next play is a screen, but I was impressed with Bell's footwork and how he put a foot in the ground to make a decisive cut past the defender: LATEST PROJECTIONS (Photo: Jeffrey Vest, Getty) ESPN's Mel Kiper: Not in 2-round mock CBS Sports' Pete Prisco: Not in 1st round mock The Ringer's Danny Kelly: Not in 1st round mock Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer: Not in 7-round mockMY PREDICTION(Photo: Benjamin Wolk, 247Sports) Bell goes 209th (6th round) to the Washington Commanders. Bell has gotten comparisons to Samuel in the past, so my projection is that Samuel's current team adds Bell to the fold. Washington needs to add receivers to make sure Jayden Daniels has more options besides Terry McLaurin. My prediction is that the Commanders take a receiver in the first or second round but take a flier on Bell on the draft's final day.PREVIOUS BREAKDOWNS
